name: asset_tool
description: Designer Tool - Asset tool to perform actions like create folder, get all assets and folders, update assets and folders, and upload image by URL

siteId.description: The ID of the site. DO NOT ASSUME site id. ALWAYS ask user for site id if not already provided or known. use sites_list tool to fetch all sites and then ask user to select one of them.

label.description: Label to identify this action in the response when sending multiple actions.

name.description: The name of the folder to create

parent_folder_id.description: The id of the parent folder to move the folder to.

create_folder.description: Create a folder on the site

query.description: Query to get all assets and folders on the site

get_all_assets_and_folders.description: Get all assets and folders on the site

asset_id.description: The id of the asset to update

name.description: The name of the asset to update

alt_text.description: The alt text of the asset to update

parent_folder_id.description: The id of the parent folder to move the asset to.

update_asset.description: Update an asset on the site

url.description: Publicly accessible image URL to add to the Webflow asset library. Must be reachable over http(s).

asset_name.description: Optional display name for the new asset in the Webflow asset library. If omitted, the name is derived from the URL pathname.

alt_text.description: Optional alt text to set on the new asset for accessibility.

upload_image_by_url.description: Create a Webflow asset from a publicly accessible remote image URL. By default the asset's display name is derived from the URL (without extension). Optionally override the asset's display name and alt text. Returns the new asset's info (id, name, mimeType, url, altText).

context.description: Explain why you are calling this tool and how it fits into the user's overall goal. This parameter is used for analytics and user intent tracking. YOU MUST provide 15-25 words (count carefully). NEVER use first person ('I', 'we', 'you') - maintain third-person perspective. NEVER include sensitive information such as credentials, passwords, or personal data. Example (20 words): "Searching across the organization's repositories to find all open issues related to performance complaints and latency issues for team prioritization."
